plan.planning_summary: Refining route_01 based on iteration 01 (score 0.955) vs iteration 05 (score 0.594) comparison. The sharp performance drop in iteration 05 stems from artificially tight thickness bounds [50,150]nm that conflict with quarter-wave optical thickness requirements at 3-5 μm wavelengths. This refinement restores physically-appropriate thickness ranges while applying feedback directives: initialize from empirical thickness manifold of successful iteration 01 candidates, center on mean ~950nm (not 95.5nm - the feedback contains a unit error, actual successful thicknesses were 400-1600nm range), apply Gaussian perturbation σ=150nm, and reduce optimizer step size by 40%. Three complementary routes test: (1) restored bounds with empirical initialization, (2) reduced layer count 18-layer for manufacturability, (3) asymmetric cavity design for improved dual-band balance.

routes.title: 22-Layer ZnS/MgF2 Dual-Band Filter with Empirical Thickness Initialization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: The iteration 05 performance degradation (0.594 vs 0.955) resulted from thickness bounds [50,150]nm being physically incompatible with quarter-wave optical thickness at 3-5 μm wavelengths. Restoring bounds to [400,1600]nm range observed in iteration 01 successful candidates, with initialization centered on empirical mean thickness ~950nm from top performers, will recover high target scores while maintaining the proven 22-layer alternating ZnS/MgF2 topology.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stack principle with alternating high/low index dielectrics; layer optical thickness approximately λ/4 at center of passbands. Empirical initialization from successful iteration 01 candidates preserves the thickness manifold that achieved 0.955 score.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [ZnS | MgF2] × 11 | CaF2 substrate; exactly 22 finite layers in alternating sequence
design_variables: All 22 layer thicknesses in nm, initialized from iteration 01 candidate mean thickness distribution with Gaussian perturbation σ=150nm
Optimizer step size reduced by 40% relative to iteration 05
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 3.25-3.35 μm and 4.20-4.30 μm passbands
Minimize mean transmittance in 2.50-3.10 μm and 4.45-5.00 μm stopbands
manufacturing_considerations: ZnS and MgF2 are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
Thickness ranges [400,1600]nm compatible with PVD deposition control
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack design principle for alternating index multilayers
Transfer matrix method for coherent thin-film interference calculation
Empirical thickness distribution from iteration 01 successful candidates
expected_advantages: Recover iteration 01 performance level (target score ~0.95) by restoring physically-appropriate thickness bounds
Empirical initialization reduces search space and prevents over-detuning
Reduced optimizer step size preserves multi-band margin feasibility
known_risks: Local optimization may converge to suboptimal thickness configuration
Spectral ripple may increase with 22-layer thickness
Deposition stress may cause thickness deviation from design
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer alternating ZnS/MgF2 multilayer filter on CaF2 substrate under normal incidence. Layer sequence: ZnS(1), MgF2(2), ZnS(3), MgF2(4), ZnS(5), MgF2(6), ZnS(7), MgF2(8), ZnS(9), MgF2(10), ZnS(11), MgF2(12), ZnS(13), MgF2(14), ZnS(15), MgF2(16), ZnS(17), MgF2(18), ZnS(19), MgF2(20), ZnS(21), MgF2(22). Initialize all 22 thicknesses from empirical mean of iteration 01 top candidates (approximately 950nm mean) with Gaussian perturbation standard deviation 150nm. Constrain thickness bounds to [400, 1600]nm per layer. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with step size reduced by 40% relative to standard. Evaluate transmittance at four wavelength bands: passbands 3250-3350nm and 4200-4300nm (maximize), stopbands 2500-3100nm and 4450-5000nm (minimize). Score via equal-weight mean aggregation across bands. Air incidence, CaF2 substrate, no metal layers, coherent TMM solver. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 2500-3100 nm, 3250-3350 nm, 4200-4300 nm, 4450-5000 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 3.25-3.35 um and 4.20-4.30 um bands; Low transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: High transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 24; No metal layers; Conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Iteration 05 thickness bounds [50,150]nm were physically incompatible with quarter-wave requirements at 3-5 μm wavelengths, causing score drop from 0.955 to 0.594. This refinement restores bounds to [400,1600]nm matching iteration 01 successful candidates, initializes from empirical thickness manifold, and reduces optimizer step size per feedback directives.

routes.title: 18-Layer ZnS/MgF2 Dual-Band Filter for Reduced Manufacturability Risk
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Reducing layer count from 22 to 18 layers will maintain acceptable dual-band performance while improving manufacturability and reducing deposition-induced stress. Evidence indicates coating thickness limits (~20-40 μm) and quality control difficulty increase with layer count. 18 layers should achieve target score >0.85 while providing margin against thickness control errors.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stack with reduced layer count; fewer layers reduce total coating thickness and deposition time while maintaining basic bandpass functionality through cavity resonance.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [ZnS | MgF2] × 9 | CaF2 substrate; exactly 18 finite layers in alternating sequence
design_variables: All 18 layer thicknesses in nm, initialized from scaled iteration 01 thickness distribution
Optimizer step size reduced by 40% relative to standard
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 3.25-3.35 μm and 4.20-4.30 μm passbands
Minimize mean transmittance in 2.50-3.10 μm and 4.45-5.00 μm stopbands

manufacturing_considerations: Reduced total thickness improves deposition quality control
ZnS and MgF2 conventional IR dielectrics
theory_basis: Layer count directly relates to coating thickness and vacuum chamber residence time
Fewer layers reduce transmissive behavior control difficulty
Quarter-wave stack principle remains valid at reduced layer count

routes.title: 22-Layer Asymmetric Cavity Design for Improved Dual-Band Balance
routes.scientific_hypothesis: The symmetric alternating ZnS/MgF2 topology may not optimally balance the two widely separated passbands (3.3 μm and 4.25 μm). Introducing asymmetric cavity structure with modified layer sequence (thicker cavity layers for longer wavelength band) will improve spectral balance between methane and CO2 bands while maintaining 22-layer count and proven material pair.
routes.design_principle: Dual-cavity bandpass filter with asymmetric cavity optical thicknesses tuned to each passband center wavelength. Cavity layers adjacent to passband centers use thicker optical thickness proportional to wavelength ratio (4.25/3.3 ≈ 1.29).
routes.proposed_topology: Air | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS(cavity1) | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS(cavity2-thick) | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS(cavity3) | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | CaF2 substrate; exactly 22 finite layers with 3 cavity layers at positions 5, 10, 15 having differentiated thickness initialization
design_variables: All 22 layer thicknesses in nm, with cavity layers (5, 10, 15) initialized 29% thicker than non-cavity layers to match 4.25/3.3 wavelength ratio
Non-cavity layers initialized from iteration 01 empirical mean ~950nm
Cavity layers initialized from iteration 01 empirical mean × 1.29 ≈ 1225nm
Gaussian perturbation σ=150nm applied to all layers
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 3.25-3.35 μm and 4.20-4.30 μm passbands with improved balance between bands
Minimize mean transmittance in 2.50-3.10 μm and 4.45-5.00 μm stopbands
Reduce passband transmission asymmetry compared to symmetric topology
manufacturing_considerations: ZnS and MgF2 conventional IR dielectrics
theory_basis: Bandpass filter construction from long-pass and short-pass combinations
Cavity optical thickness proportional to center wavelength for resonance
Dual-cavity design enables multiple transmission bands
expected_advantages: Improved transmission balance between 3.3 μm and 4.25 μm passbands
Better stopband blocking through cavity resonance tuning
Maintains 22-layer manufacturability while improving spectral performance
Asymmetric initialization may escape local optima of symmetric topology
known_risks: Asymmetric design may introduce spectral ripple asymmetry
Cavity thickness differentiation may reduce overall transmission
Optimization may converge to symmetric solution negating asymmetric initialization benefit
